tier.title: Tier
tier.description: The tier that produced these numbers.

limited.title: Limited
limited.description: Whether this deployment limits anything at all. False on a self-hosted server that has configured nothing, where every allowance below is unlimited.

LimitsOut.title: LimitsOut
LimitsOut.description: Everything this server allows the calling household.

resource.title: Resource
resource.description: The resource this allowance governs, e.g. 'recipes'.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: How many are allowed, or null for unlimited. This is the number the household will actually meet: whichever of its tier's cap and this server's fair-use ceiling is lower.

used.title: Used
used.description: How many exist now, or null where the number has no meaning: an unlimited allowance (nothing was counted), or one scoped to a single meal or plan rather than the household.

remaining.title: Remaining
remaining.description: limit - used, floored at zero; null whenever either is null.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Where the allowance applies: 'per household', 'in one meal', 'a month'.

upgradable.title: Upgradable
upgradable.description: Whether a larger tier on this server would raise this limit. False for a fair-use ceiling, for the largest tier, and for a server that sells nothing.

ResourceAllowanceOut.title: ResourceAllowanceOut
ResourceAllowanceOut.description: What this household is allowed of one resource, and how much is spent.

AdhocItemIn.title: AdhocItemIn
AdhocItemIn.description:
Ad-hoc addition (the milk-is-out case). Clients may supply their own
item id — offline-first iOS creates the item locally and syncs later, and
a retrying AI won't double-add (idempotent by id).
